items.title: Billy Taylor — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So they had their Clarence Cameron whites and they had all of these people that had excelled in the European tradition but only as soloists

ctx.x: That is not an isolated incident. If I can say most African American Colleges at that time had that kind of value system. Why do you think that was?

And still do, too many of them, have the same thing. It is ongoing. It has never changed in most schools. It never changed because, I think, they felt, many of the people who had studied, if they lived in Mississippi or any of the southern schools, they had been sent to white schools because they couldn’t go to [Unintelligible] or the University of Arkansas or to North Carolina, the white schools in North Carolina or wherever. So what they learned from this was that to be competitive you had to beat the white man…
were organized here in New York by Wilmarian Cook and James [Unintelligible] and people like that.
